reviews.text: Game Name: Age of Defense Release[Early Access]: 27 May, 2019 Game Type/Genre: Tower Defense. Theme: Cartoon, fantasy, Stone Age. Difficulty: Average. AI: Dumb as a rock. Pros: +Funny cartoon style graphics +Background music is enjoyable +Several different towers. +Several different enemies. +Did I mention Boss fights?:) +Easy to learn. +Can Run on a potato. +Price. Cons: -Too short (only 4 missions available atm) -No achivmets. -No trading cards. Overall it is a fine game to skip some time.

A new game from the already familiar team that specializes in Tower Defense games. A little strange graphic menu, drawn in the style of ancient cave drawings, but after a couple of mouse clicks, everything becomes clear and simple. Cool animated intro before each level, drawn in the same ancient cave style. Music - made with high quality, it is unobtrusive. The gameplay is a little bit similar to other TD games, but all the same has differences. The player has several different game units with different speeds and different defeat strengths. Units can be put on almost any place, for them there are no fixed places. Still, the player has access to various additional means of killing monsters, for example: you can drop a stone on them or put sharp wooden stakes in their way. And the stone lying on the road prevents the monsters from moving forward, and your units have the opportunity to destroy them while they are standing still. In the game there are many types of sympathetic monsters that sometimes come out of the most unexpected places. Sometimes bosses crawl out, which is not so easy to destroy. One of the most important advantages of the game - the minimum requirements for hardware. The only things that did not like: the blood of the monsters which is not absorbed into the ground and slightly acidic and very unusual colors of the environment. Otherwise, I was very pleased with this game and recommend it for purchase.

Entertaining and charming tower defense game that did not disappoint. Overall a very solid, simple design, with charming, well made art. The game with it`s amazing cartoonish style graphics and excellent response it`s definetly a must play, if you`re into tower defense games. The player has several game units with different speeds, fun to use and also seem better thought out. The difficulty scales nicely and always something different about the next level to keep you interested. A very solid experience overall, and I look forward to any future updates.

本评测写于v0.51.0beta版本，暂时只有4个关卡，三种难度。我难度2通关，第一关难度3过了。 这是一款很有潜力的类Kingdom Rush的优秀塔防游戏 [h1]前言[/h1] 这是我第一次很认真很正式的于STEAM写游戏评测。 一次巧合，一次美丽的邂逅。 晚饭时随手翻QQ群，正好看到拼包群有人招募写评论PY游戏key，并有群友回复连youtubers life都能通过写评论得到。提起了我的兴趣，点了几个游戏链接，发现大多游戏都是我喜欢的类型，于是长年潜水的我厚着脸皮联系并得到了这款游戏的key。 [h1]正文[/h1] 首先是涂鸦画风的史前时代片头，简洁不简单，音乐真的超级棒！ 画风和著名塔防游戏Kingdom Rush的风格很像，从某方面来说可以媲美Kingdom Rush，售价亦相近。 单单目前就可以很愉快的玩上2-3个小时。 ++ 音乐真的特别棒，超级喜欢。 +++ 怪物，地形机制的设计脑洞大开，惊艳不已 + 贴心的设计，游戏右下角可以拉扯防止挡到建筑图标。关卡的图标设计都是按动物的进化史来的。 - 一些BUG，轻微影响游戏体验 - 难度3下，怪物防御，血量太高，塔防的平衡，性价比调整得不好。 ---------‘不合理’ 游戏完全没有文字，因为史前人类还不会书写是吗：）所以第一关的教程几乎没存在感。 并且有一个疑似BUG的地方，开局教程提示造投矛手，后续的投石，减速，以及最重要的尖刺陷阱魔法大概率会卡住很多轮次才出现！ 我多次重开游戏，有时候第一轮怪，这些塔和魔法就出现了。 可以通过点击出怪口的骷髅头图标直接刷新一波怪，但没有任何奖励，只是减少等待而已。遇到过出怪倒计时完成却不出怪的BUG，卡了大概10秒。 魔法有充能冷却以及有效时间，超过时间会消失。充能满了不释放不会额外充能次数。 释放尖刺魔法明明是一个方块范围，却只给了一个小圆点的释放目标，很难准确释放在需要的地方，怪物走道很随意可能不会踩，白白浪费。而难度3下，魔法是通关与否的最重要因素。 投石和投矛性价比差异太大，特别在难度3的第一关。 目前版本想通关难度3只能靠拖延时间用尖刺魔法活活磨死高级怪。 建筑的图标颜色太暗淡，无法出售建筑。 ---------‘真香’ 因为一开始我就玩难度3和难度2，加上BUG等不合理的体验在前。 第2关的各种怪物特色，地形特殊机制，以及最后BOSS的出场方式真的惊艳到我了！！制作方的创意真的太棒了，所以我喜欢上了这款游戏，对以后的更新充满了期待。 有机制地形‘吞噬腔体’它会偶尔吞噬路过的怪物然后在另一边的道路吐出很多的小怪物！ 有的怪物会有多种形态，比如大甲虫死了孵化小甲虫。肉虫子躲在别的怪的掩护下。走路很快的怪物，受到攻击会减速蹲走减少伤害。以及第三关的陆地改飞行怪，不受到攻击就迅速回满血量的怪物。 这些都很考验玩家的塔类选择以及建造的位置，适当地提高了难度和成就感。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

Age of defense [h1] 游戏简介 [/h1] Age of defense 中文名 防御时代 ，一个远古时代为背景的塔防游戏，你身为一个部落的统治者，你需要保护你的人民。 [h1] 游戏玩法[/h1] 玩家可以通过肉棒的数量来部署你的部落勇士来防御远古生物的进攻，每关貌似都会解锁一些技能，供你使用。 [h1]游戏优点[/h1] 远古生物是有碰撞体积，所以你可以通过在路上设置障碍物来干扰敌人。没有强行规定防御工事的摆放地点，你可以把它放在你想放的地方。 [h1]游戏缺点[/h1] 关卡太少，没有新手教程，防御工事种类没有进步（简单说就是抄了同类塔防的工事种类）。 [h1]游戏总体评价[/h1] 如果你同类塔防都通关的话，不妨来试试这个，如果没有，不建议购买这款，主要问题就是关卡太少了,其他还Ok.

Let me start by saying that this is not a bad game at all... it's more like a multitude of little things that prevent me from endorsing this game. It plays alright, the grafics fit and the maps look nice - also i was a huge fan of the previous game from this developer. BUT: - Some times you have no chance of knowing which path enemies will take, giving you a sure loss the first time you play the map. - It is near impossible to know where the hitbox of flying units is and thus almost impossible to place your anti air towers correctly - To me it does not feel satisfying to kill enemies... specially in the first few levels it feels like playing a losing battle against way to tough monsters and all you can do is prevent losing the game - dont dream about perfect runs... feels like shooting peas at mudcrabs. - So far there are too few towers to choose from, making it hard to find "your favourite tower", which to me is a bad thing.. i like my little favourites, or pet projects and see them grow along the way. - No permanent evolving - the unlocks you get are on a per level basis (which is nice in a way that you can specialize anew for each level - but robs you of that progress feeling) and unlocked towers are only unlocked from that point forward, so no going back to levels you found hard with your new towers or passive unlocks. It is near impossible to understand what the hell your unlocks do... i get that having only pictograms and no text in the game is a feature and a cool one at that... MOST OF THE TIME, i dont think having a mandatory help button that opens a steam community site with descriptions is the right way to go - maybe have the community help out with suggestions and bring the good ones into the game instead. Let me end this by saying: I really want to like this game, but at this point i cannot YET. ----------------- Update: After playing through all available levels i stand by my original assessment - The game is by no means bad and has a lot of potential as it grows, but as of now i sadly cannot recommend buying it because of all the aforementioned problems.

If you like Tower Defence games such as the Kingdom Rush series, then this would be the game for you as the cartoony graphics, gameplay and style are similar. The big difference though is that this developer has pushed out an early access game that still requires a lot of work and they do not seem to take constructive player feedback too well either. So, I do not recommend this early access game. The real bull****: When I saw this game advertised on Steam, the look and feel reminded me of Kingdom Rush. I was super pumped as Ironhide Studios (the makers of Kingdom Rush) make epic TD games, so naturally, I was excited about the possibility of new developers re-inventing the TD wheel with a similar feel. Boy was I wrong! The game takes you back, waaaaaay back to the caveman era...you know, before wheels and tasty cheeses and even Tim Tams and it seems that the developers thought it might be only fitting to remove all the text from the entire game as well, making you groan and scratch your head (like a cave person) as you try to figure out how to get through the game as everything is in Hieroglyphics... I mean, like everything! The menu, the partly upgrade-able tech tree and all the levels, all in weird picture forms (which only worsens the frustration when you keep dying on levels because you partially think it's your fault that you selected the picture of the monkey when maybe you should have selected the pointing arrows instead. I would like to think that I am a bit of a TD wizard and started this game out on the hard, difficulty setting as I do enjoy a good challenge. Let me just say that after almost 3 hours of gameplay, repeating levels over and over again (because I was dying...a lot!!), trying to figure out many possible defence patterns and even reducing the settings down to the easiest mode, I was ready to act like a cave person in wanting to throw my monitor over the side of the balcony in frustration. The only patterns that I found was where other gamers were sharing their same frustration on the developers' discussion boards here on steam. So, I joined them. I shared my views with the developers on what worked, what didn't work (which is most of the game), bugs, positive suggestions on how to improve the game experience and finally, that if they were to fix anything at all, that it would be just these two things; - Realigning the difficulty settings (as even on the easiest setting, players were not getting passed the first 5 or so levels) which they have said that they have done, but they need to revisit this. - Including text (like human beings) so that players would be able to understand how the tech tree works, the menu and so on. I do not know of any other new-age games that have no tutorials or descriptions on gameplay, tech tree and menus at all, like ever! The result thus far: After much back and forth with the developers in the Steam discussion posts (and even having to raise my voice sometimes, which is really just me using a few CAPS and inserting some **** here and there), the developers finally expressed that they would lower the games difficulty settings and make it easier (although they thought this request was so silly because they didn't think that game was challenging at all on easy mode). For those of you who think that you're up for a challenge, I invite you to purchase the game, play it for no more than 2 hours (so that you can request a refund from Steam, because trust me, you will!) and you can see what the rest of us are talking about. After the developers' so-called 'changes,' I have since replayed a couple of levels and I have noticed that they have increased the number of lives that you get when starting a level, but the game is still challenging and it is not fun to play anymore, because you still die and are frequently outnumbered. For example: On the 6th level, on the easiest setting, I have towers set up in almost every possible inch of space available and by wave 20 (of 28 waves), the maps are overrun with monsters and makes it feel impossible to complete. The towers are not strong enough to control the hordes and the upgrades are so expensive that you will die before being able to save up enough money to even start upgrading. TD games are supposed to be fun because you get to control and choose what towers go where, and you choose how and when to upgrade them. If these developers have designed only one or two correct building patterns in order to gain success, then the game does not really provide a unique game experience and I, for one, am not patient enough to sit through another 10+ hours in trying to figure that out and dying, like, 100 more times. Summary: The game has potential, but the developers need to realise that we, the players tell you what we do not like about the game, not because we are angry inside and are training to become a keyboard warriors, but because we like the concept, we want to support you and we want to maximise our gaming experience. And I am aware that developers are not there to cater to the needs of everyone, but when the cries are all the same, you would think the developers would see that as a big enough warning. If I were you, I would save your money, for now, and your sanity (as this game will most certainly test your more than just your patience) and wait until the developers take the time to cater to players needs. Fixes: 1. Text is a crucial part to understanding any game. You cannot expect players to literally have to think like a caveman. Even the latest VR games are not that muted or self-explanatory. We get that you are trying to create a caveman-like theme, but you kinda lose that feeling when you are outnumbered by waves of flying fish, alien monsters and magical wizards. 2. Decrease the difficulty settings. We have gone back and forth about this one before over the last 2 weeks with you, yet you seem to think we are like new to gaming or something. It is frustrating to have to continue to request this from you. Easy means easy, so stop creating ridiculous amounts of waves that outnumber the players' towers and lower your settings so that for those who choose the easy setting, could complete the game with their eyes closed! It's as 'easy' as that! 3. The buttons on the screen are all over the place (mainly in the far, four corners) and often cover the towers in the game. It would be great if you have a little side pocket that would slide over into the screen when you hover over it or zooming out from the map so that you can fit all of the towers and buttons on the screen. 4. You should allow for shortcut button for power-ups so that the two (or three) that are available, can be selected by pressing the numbers 1, 2 or 3 on the keyboard. Having to click on a power-up and then dragging the mouse all the way over to the area that you want to activate the power-up, is pretty ****** and can sometimes cause you to lose lives, as sometimes placing a power-up one second early, may have saved a few lives. 5. Create more roads to allow for more towers. I can share screenshots where I have towers covering all the available roads along the path and many of the monsters still manage to get all the way through, so die of course, but each wave, I lose lives and over time, I am outnumbered. 6. Lower the cost of upgrades or increase the amount of money that you get when killing monsters. Your basic tower costs $35. To upgrade it twice costs over $250. When you consider that killing a monster returns only a few dollars each, it is very difficult to end up upgrading all the towers over the course of the level. 7. Increase the tower's damage. It is frustrating when you spend over $300 building and upgrading a wizards tower only to realise that the wizard does not actually do that much more damage from when it was first built to when it ti fully upgraded. 8. If you choose to ignore the above suggestions, then you should reduce the number of monsters per wave.

[code]Written By Hidden Gems Review : https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38624426/[/code] Age of Defense is a really nice tower defense. It's like any other tower defense pretty addictive you upgrade towers you kill monsters running well fluid and consistent, and the art looks good. But all that good stuff I said don't match with the crappy interface and bugs that make the game nearly unplayable in some stages, that make you can't move on to the next stage... You can see a gameplay here : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ELFR3VnQh6g&t

EDIT: Ive now played all the levels - or at least tried them. This game needs serious balance, especially in the first 6 levels. It is WAY too difficult (on normal) by the third and fourth levels. - Too many mobs, too little money for towers. - This is only compounded by the complete lack of explaination for abilities, upgrades and the skill tree. The devs linked a faq page about these things on steam discussions but not only do I not want to have to have that open just to play a stupid game, it's also not completely accurate! I'm still not sure wtf the fish woman tower does on the various upgrades! Bottom line, had I known the devs were still working on Warstone I would not have purchased this. Learn from the recent failures of the Battlefield franchise and finish one game before releasing another. OG Review: This game needs some polish. Even with the benefit of the doubt I still have to give it a bad review for now but the issues it has are completely fixable, largely QOL things! The issues - No hotkeys! Wanna place a tower? Gotta click it. Wanna drop a spike/nuke? (Which you'll do about every 10 seconds) GOTTA MOUSE OVER TO THE BOTTOM LEFT AND CLICK THAT SUCKA THEN AIM IT! Please just f*cking put towers on 1-4 and the extra ditties on q,w,e etc. Very easy QOL fix!! - CAN'T SELL TOWERS. I didn't think this was much of an issue at first but wow by the time you get to the third level and fight the giant.... octopus... thing? The issue becomes clear quickly. You fight one tentacle at a time while battling absolute hoards of smaller mobs then that tentacle dies and another one sprouts. The problem is you are required to place a tower or two in a weird corner of the map to fight said tentacle only to have that tower sit there, useless, the rest of the fight.... Now multiply that by 3. I call that ARTIFICALLLLL DIFFICULTYYYY!! - The language barrier This is the low hanging fruit of the complaints. I don't think the symbols are THAT bad but they are not that great either. The fact that you have to have a separate web page open to read the sill tree is... mmm.. not exactly what people want in a seemingly simple TD game. If you're gonna copy Kingdom Rush so blatantly (which is not a problem in itself) at least follow the winning formula they have and KEEP IT SIMPLE, STUPID!
I'm disappointed to say that it's a VERY HARD, ugly and poor version of Kingdom Rush. Just go play the original :(

Neat art style, but it's animated at like 15FPS or lower, so it doesn't look as nice as it could be. "The path is blockable" - I'm on level 5 of 9 levels and I have only one way to block the path. It's a tiny boulder, it lasts for a very short duration and has a really long cooldown. It doesn't really stop the flow of the enemies on the path. "No buildfields!" - But there might as well be, because there is so much non-removable blocking objects in the world that limit where you can place towers. "Epic Boss fights" - I've encountered one so far, and while it was interesting, it was impossible to plan for until you played through the level at least once. Which just means replaying the level. "12 unique towers" - I think this includes the upgraded versions, since I only have 4 towers half way through the game. The costs of the base towers and their upgrades made it restrictive in what you could do. Making the best strategy to just place the first tower you get everywhere and then upgrade them as you can afford. "Over 50 enemies with various abilities" - There were quite a few different looking enemies, but they mostly all functioned the same way. There were only a couple that actually did anything other than move down the path. None of the towers, abilities, talents, or any other UI elements have text, so it's impossible to tell what something does. The abilities are pretty much required to win, you need to spam them as often as they are available, but they sometimes fail to work on the first click and you have to click again. The abilities also work in build areas, for some reason, and may even cause the build areas to no longer allow building in them. You have the option of making a wave of enemies appear right away instead of waiting for the timer to complete, but you don't get anything for doing it, so you might as well not do it. When you get talents is completely random. One level you might get one on wave 3, another level you might get it on wave 10. There is no indicators as to when you are going to get one. Additionally, there is no info on how many you will get on a level, so you can't plan ahead.

[b]Edit:[/b] This review was written for an earlier version of the game. I haven't played it since recent updates, so some aspects of the game might have improved. This game really annoyed me. Mainly because it does some things right, so you want it to be good, but it just leaves you frustrated. [b]The Good Part:[/b] -Art style and animations are quite nice. -Some creative enemies that you need to plan around. [b]The Medium Part:[/b] -This game has no text, only symbols. I like the idea, but I feel like it's not really working. If you've never played a tower defense game before, do definitely not start here. You'll have no clue what to do. [b]The Frustrating Part:[/b] -As said, this game contains no text, which means you get very little explanation to start the game. If you've played Kingdom Rush or the like before you'll recognize some basic towers to get started, but if you've never played a TD before, I imagine this would be a very frustrating experience. -At some point it was possible to upgrade your units. I had to play that level a second time to find out [i]how[/i] because the upgrade button was awkwardly placed and barely visible if too expensive. -At some point you get a skill tree which resets every level. I do not know when you get skill points. You can't know what those perks do unless you click on the icon which leads you to a list on steam in your browser. If you want to know what perk you're choosing you have to switch between the game and browser. This just seems like bad design to me. -It's hard to see where the enemies are coming from and where they're going. In one map I had to restart because there was another exit hidden behind the tower icons. You couldn't scroll down far enough to properly see what was going on. -Sometimes you'll get an achievement. What it's for? No idea, unless you look up the description on steam because the title of the achievement is, again, just symbols. -Even on the easiest difficulty enemies will come through. I'm not inexperienced when it comes to TDs, but I can't finish the early levels on easy flawlessly, which feels weird. You start with 75 lives and you don't get a grade on how many lives you've got left, so I'm guessing this is by design. For me it's just frustrating. If ten enemies come through at once, you'd think you're doing something wrong, but I just couldn't figure out what. Spamming the active abilities helps, but I feel like they shouldn't be that necessary in a TD. I would maybe expect this for later stages of the game, but not the first three levels on easiest. [b]Conclusion:[/b] I don't think I'll be playing this game again soon. There are TDs out there that are so much better and less frustrating. I might give it a try when it's out of early access, but in the current state I can't really recommend this game to anyone. [b]To the Devs:[/b] Please just add some text, even if it was only for the skill tree. And maybe some balancing too. This game has great potential, I like the idea of no text, but I think you're taking it too far and the game suffers from it. [b]Tl;dr:[/b] Game is hard, has no explanations and feels incredibly frustrating. Play Kingdom Rush, Gemcraft, Creeper World, Dungeon Warfare or any other Tower Defense instead.

Having had problems with the game previously and seeing it was updated I decided to give it another go. I started the game and wanted to reset my progress. Well, you would think that would be easy wouldn't you? Not with a menu system written for an autist. I finally found a thread in the discussions and was able to do it but to have to search there for something so basic really sums up why the menu idea is so bad. So, before I've even begun playing again, I already have a bad taste in my mouth. How do you do it? Press alt-ctrl-numpad5 in game then quit to the main menu. Very intuitive. Now let's get to the game. To be fair, I can't stand tower defence games, but Warstone TD actually changed my mind, and as this is from the same dev, you would think you would know what to expect, right? Wrong. The same autistic menu system is in game and the gameplay is ruined by it. I can't tell what changes or improvements have been made because it feels and plays exactly how I remember it, badly, and I can see why I hated it the first time around. The first level is very colourful, almost like a technicolour yawn. It starts with waves of "red dots". Red dots! Is that the best you could come up with? You watch the red dots, while you just sit there and twiddle your thumbs adding units as they become available, the very reason I hate tower defence personified and being Australian I couldn't switch off that cringeworthy background music fast enough. Oh, and you get to place crosses on the path which I assume are some sort of pointy (pointless) defence system. After the first level, I selected the second level from the menu and it crashed back to the OS. That was enough for me. I'll stick to Warstone TD. This isn't just a step backwards, it's a giant leap in evolutionary development in reverse. So finally all I can say is, "Into the trash it goes". TL;DR: Just NO.

[h1] Disclamer: I changed my review based on developer feedback in the comments [/h1] Here are my reasons why you should wait on this game and check back in when more updates are released. I've been around the block when it comes to TD games in every genre and this game is pretty straight forward. Some positives to take away are that the art direction and the general 'feel' of the game are pretty neat and the concept is definitely one of a kind. 1. [b] Bugs [/b]. I've encounter a total of 34 bugs having only played for 10 hours. With each new revision of this game it seems like the devs add new bugs while not addressing any previous issues. The talent tree is completely broken (clicking on talents sometimes does not work), enemies get stuck on everything and can be bugged out of the pathing area, etc. 3. [b] There is no game balance [/b]. I can't tell which tower type goes against which enemy type. Even if that were apparent the game throws so many enemies at you it makes all single target towers irrelevant when there are 100+ enemies in one wave. Some enemies have special abilities when they get hit a la speeding up when hit by an aoe, but this just causes the game to become needlessly tedious and frustrating. The aoe tower is essentially the only one you will ever need with one occasional single target tower. 4. [b] Difficulty is just an illusion [/b]. The harder the difficulty the less lives you have to spare for each wave. However, the same amount of waves and enemies are thrown at you. So the enemies will still be just as tough on wave 8 on easy as they are on wave 8 on hard. You'll just be able to get to the next wave on easy before losing all your lives because you have more to spare. 4. [b] Less is not more [/b]. The game leans on the fact that you are playing in 2000 B.C. and no written language is given. Thus, menu options are given as caveman (and cavewomen!) artwork to help navigation, as well as what enemies are vulnerable to. This is a very neat and cute concept [i] AT FIRST [/i] but then gets old real fast real quick. I think if the menu options and the story overall were given in the show don't tell format that would be great, I would just want what the different enemy types and vulnerabilities are to be laid out in plain [insert your language here]. 5. [b] The talent tree is nonsensical [/b]. There is too much going on in the talent tree, with the placement of progression nodes I can't tell what leads into what or how many points it takes to get there or what's even good. I can't tell if the sniper tree attribute in the aoe tree will also to help with the actual sniper tree in the single target spear tree. I can't tell why I'm not able to progress past a certain point in the tree with the cost of all talents being 99 when I only have 18 thus far. I don't get what the hints are or how to figure them out I guess. I understand that I can be a bit of a caveman myself when it comes to grasping some of these concepts but this game needed to be polished quite a bit more before it was released. TLDR; Game needs some work; developers are working on it and are responsive (see coments); I'll update my review in a few months with the updates coming out.

I bought this game 5 years ago (Yes, in 2019) when it first was in early access. I bought it because Warstone, Battlecruisers first game, is one of my favorite games. I installed it a few times over the past years but the game did not seem to make any real indepth progress. So I was surprised to see that it came out of early access. So I installed it for the fifth time. Conclusion: Age of Defence does not even come close to Warstone. It seems to have been programmed by a completely different team of developers. The game comes with almost no explanation, has a very bad interface with useless tooltips. There is no monster encyclopedia or detailed information on the towers and development paths. No tutorial. The menus block the playing field. The help button points to a website with zero help for new players. And completely outdated videos. Sure, there is a really good game somewhere underneath this mess, but there is still an awful lot of work to be done. Should never have left early access in this state...

Fortunately, seems that developers fixes things from time to time. To finish campaing in all modes with 100% achievements takes more of 100 hours. Recommedable for children, newbies or casuals.

【防御纪元】Age of Defense简称AOD。主要关卡15×3（45个关卡），每个关均有挑战任务，相当于45×3（135关/次）又臭又长。 游戏方面：以最高难度为主，抽象的不能再抽象，目前玩过最难的塔防游戏。防御塔也不能出售，不能通过卖塔变现支援其他路。 不开倍速，前期就奔着半小时一把了，后期更是1个多小时，有倍速才控制到半小时左右。怪物数量极其逆天，N3模式的怪比我钱都多。 逆天索敌，逆天路线，逆天怪量，各种bug。所有防御塔都不会优先索敌空军，就导致一群人搁那刮痧大怪，都不愿意去打一斧子秒杀的空军，高质量怪海里空军几乎必漏。 还有滑翔伞的怪+逆天路线，从我家门口刷怪，打下来后掉到家门口，直接进去了，不会跟其他怪一样顺着路走下去，也不会按照飞行前的路线继续行走。哪怕后期全科技部分关卡都打的坐牢，能打过，但是打的太难受了，n3模式真的太穷了。 以及各种bug，打完了怪不出来，因为怪在地图外，那你造塔啊，不好意思塔不能卖，没位置造投矛手了 反正就是一坨，能玩，但建议低难度体验，不然纯坐大牢。

A nice take on a Tower Defense Game, with caveman era towers and evolving threats emerging from the seas along with a nice variety of levels and upgrades for you to sink your prehistoric teeth into. It also has great visuals matching the art style of the kingdom rush franchise. I got the game a while back (not to long after the release) and at first it was hard to understand the primitive caveman images as there was still no actual text to the game you had to guess what you were clicking on, and has some bugs and issues to get passed. Since then the developers have put in the extra hours to make a solid game, I contacted them a couple of times with bugs to fix which they were actively doing and they kindly allow me some extra keys of Age of Defense and Warstone TD to give away to the community live on twitch. (I may still have a couple left if you want to try the game) They increased the upgrades for the towers tenfold and there is a great array of towers and upgrades to choose from, all the achievements are working and the difficulty scaling seems bob on. All in all a great TD game to add to your steam collection. I have over 100+ TD games in my library alone.
